equation_request.abstract: Continuous time quantum walks provide an important framework for designing new algorithms and modelling quantum transport and state transfer problems. Often, the graph representing the structure of a problem contains certain symmetries that confine the dynamics to a smaller subspace of the full Hilbert space. In this work, we use invariant subspace methods, that can be computed systematically using Lanczos algorithm, to obtain the reduced set of states that encompass the dynamics of the problem at hand without the specific knowledge of underlying symmetries. First, we apply this method to obtain new instances of graphs where the spatial quantum search algorithm is optimal: complete graphs with broken links and complete bipartite graphs, in particular, the star graph. These examples show that regularity and high-connectivity are not needed to achieve optimal spatial search. We also show that this method considerably simplifies the calculation of quantum transport efficiencies. Furthermore, we observe improved efficiencies by removing a few links from highly symmetric graphs. Finally, we show that this reduction method also allows us to obtain an upper bound for the fidelity of a single qubit transfer on an XY spin network.

specification.problem: Use Lanczos-generated invariant (Krylov) subspaces to reduce continuous-time quantum walk dynamics on symmetric graphs, illustrated by spatial search on a small graph.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background Lanczos/Krylov reduction of a CTQW Hamiltonian from an initial state, plus a tiny assumed instance: spatial search with H = -gamma*L - |w><w| on the complete graph K_N, reduced to a 2D subspace. Out of scope: broken-link complete graphs, complete bipartite/star graphs, transport efficiencies, and the XY spin network fidelity bound.

symbols.meaning: Hamiltonian of the continuous-time quantum walk
Lanczos basis vectors spanning the invariant subspace

equations.label: Lanczos recursion
equations.description: Generates an orthonormal basis of the Krylov space span{H^m psi_0}; terminates when beta=0, giving an invariant subspace.
equations.justification: The abstract names the Lanczos algorithm for computing invariant subspaces; this is the standard recursion, not paper-specific detail.

equations.label: Reduced dynamics
equations.description: Dynamics restricted to d-dimensional subspace with tridiagonal T (diagonal alpha_j, off-diagonal beta_j).
equations.justification: Follows from the invariance of the Krylov space under H.

equations.label: Assumed search Hamiltonian
equations.latex: H=-\gamma L-|w\rangle\langle w|,\quad L=N|s\rangle\langle s|\text{-complement: }L=N I-J,\ |s\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_x|x\rangle
equations.description: Spatial search Hamiltonian on K_N, with L the graph Laplacian and J the all-ones matrix, so L=N(I-|s><s|).
equations.justification: Chosen as smallest instance of spatial search; the abstract only says search is optimal on complete graphs with broken links, not this exact form.
assumptions: Full complete graph without broken links

equations.label: Reduced 2D basis
equations.latex: \mathrm{span}\{|w\rangle,|s\rangle\},\quad H|_{2D}=\begin{pmatrix}-1-\gamma N(1-1/N)&\gamma N/\sqrt{N}\\ \gamma\sqrt{N}&-\gamma N\end{pmatrix}\text{ in basis }\{|w\rangle,|w^\perp\rangle\}
equations.description: Starting from |s>, the Krylov space is spanned by |s> and |w>. Matrix is given in a non-orthonormal-to-Lanczos but schematic basis and must be recomputed with Lanczos.
equations.justification: Illustrative only; explicit matrix entries should be recomputed by eq_1 for the instance.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Encodes vertex label in computational basis (assumed)

steps.description: Choose a small N, marked vertex w, and gamma; build H.
Run Lanczos from |s> to get the invariant subspace and tridiagonal T.
Evolve in the reduced subspace and track the overlap with |w>.

specification.measurement: Computational basis measurement of the vertex register to estimate probability of w (assumed).
